text:
B: Hi! Oh, hello, can you hear me okay?
A: Erm, yeah, hi. Sorry, I think I'm a bit quiet. Is that better?
B: Yeah, that's perfect. I'm Hannah. How are you doing?
A: I'm okay, thanks. Bit tired. I'm Harriet. How are you?
B: I'm good, thanks, bit knackered. I've had a full week on placement, so I'm sort of running on biscuits. I'm doing a PGCE in Exeter, primary. I'm in a Year 1 class at the moment.
A: Oh, that's nice. Is it nice? I mean, I imagine it's quite full on.
B: It is full on, but they're so funny. One of them told me today that my ponytail looked like a horse's bottom. Which, fair. [laughs] What about you, are you a student as well?
A: Yeah, I'm in my final year at Queen Mary, history. I'm doing a dissertation on women's lodging houses in Victorian East London.
B: Oh wow, that sounds really interesting. How's it going?
A: Erm. Honestly, not great. It's due in May and I'm about a third of the way through, maybe less. I've already had one extension, so.
B: Oh no. Do you have, like, a plan for it? Sorry, I'm the person who colour-codes everything, I can't help it.
A: [laughs] No, I don't, really. I keep saying I'm going to make one. I just sort of sit down and then it's been two hours and I've read about lodging-house regulations from 1851 and written nothing. If that makes sense.
B: No, it does. I think everyone's got their thing. Mine's, I can't start anything until I've got the plan, so I spend ages laminating stuff at the kitchen table instead. My mum's like, Hannah, that's not lesson planning, that's arts and crafts.
A: That's still more productive than me.
B: [laughs] Do you work as well, or is it just the uni?
A: I do a couple of shifts at a secondhand bookshop in Walthamstow. I found a Barbara Pym first edition last week for two pounds, which I was quite pleased about.
B: Is that a good one? Sorry, I don't really know her.
A: Erm, she's sort of, quiet novels about church people and spinsters in the fifties. Very funny, actually, in a dry way. I don't know, it's probably not for everyone.
B: Church people, I'd probably be in one of them, then. I help run the kids' group at our church on Sundays. That's sort of what got me into teaching, really.
A: Oh, really? That's lovely. I did Sunday school growing up, and youth group. I've been meaning to find a church in Walthamstow for about a year and I just haven't.
B: Aw. It's hard when you move, isn't it? I'm lucky, I'm back home with my mum and dad, so it's just the same one I've always gone to.
A: Yeah. I do miss it, actually. More than I'd say to people at uni.
B: I get that. My uni friends don't really ask, so I don't really bring it up. I saw your photo, by the way, the bookcase. Is that all yours?
A: Mostly. My boyfriend keeps saying we need another one. We have the same one, I think, as everyone in London.
B: [laughs] Mine's a noticeboard with my netball fixtures on it, so it's a bit less intellectual.
A: You play netball? I did a term at uni in first year and then just sort of stopped going.
B: Wing attack, Tuesday nights. We lost again this week to a team we always lose to. You should give it another go, honestly, it's
A: I mean, maybe after May.
